audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. SVR sample constraints neither guarantee neighborhood retrieval nor identify the stated softmax optimizer; The printed retrieval-error bound is violated within its stated memory neighborhood; Sparse retrieval can have larger error than dense retrieval, invalidating dependent proof steps.
limitations: 0199-P1 — SVR sample constraints neither guarantee neighborhood retrieval nor identify the stated softmax optimizer — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Finite-sample SVR generalization may be studied under additional regularity and uniform approximation assumptions; these are not the universal guarantee stated.

0199-P1 — SVR sample constraints neither guarantee neighborhood retrieval nor identify the stated softmax optimizer — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Adding the natural bound on the second slack family does not repair the explicit linear example.

0199-P1 — SVR sample constraints neither guarantee neighborhood retrieval nor identify the stated softmax optimizer — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The exponential kernel expansion itself is valid, but does not determine the learned dual coefficients.

0199-P2 — The printed retrieval-error bound is violated within its stated memory neighborhood — Counterevidence and alternative readings: This is not an OCR ambiguity or a missing retained-target assumption.

0199-P2 — The printed retrieval-error bound is violated within its stated memory neighborhood — Counterevidence and alternative readings: A query-dependent score-gap bound is available for uncontaminated memories, but it is a different statement and does not establish the noisy theorem or downstream corollaries.

0199-P3 — Sparse retrieval can have larger error than dense retrieval, invalidating dependent proof steps — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The sparse target probability is higher; that alone cannot order vector-valued errors because removed distractors may cancel.

0199-P3 — Sparse retrieval can have larger error than dense retrieval, invalidating dependent proof steps — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The report does not declare the general fixed-point statement false: it identifies failure of the supplied comparison-based proof and distinguishes convergence to a nearby fixed point from convergence to the stored memory.

0199-P3 — Sparse retrieval can have larger error than dense retrieval, invalidating dependent proof steps — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Same-input error comparison, even if true, cannot directly compare different trajectories.

0199-P4 — The stated radius makes the capacity proof's separation condition impossible — Counterevidence and alternative readings: A freely chosen smaller radius can avoid this algebraic incompatibility but changes the stated radius and requires a new capacity argument.

0199-P4 — The stated radius makes the capacity proof's separation condition impossible — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The calculation invalidates the presented derivation, not the possible existence of exponential capacity under other hypotheses or arguments.

0199-P4 — The stated radius makes the capacity proof's separation condition impossible — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The full-support case avoids possible ambiguity about the radius over masked versus all memories.

0199-P5 — Released sparse kernels assign positive mass to excluded memories — Counterevidence and alternative readings: The code also contains other dense/sparsemax modules, but these do not correct the inspected sparse branch imports.

0199-P5 — Released sparse kernels assign positive mass to excluded memories — Counterevidence and alternative readings: This establishes a defect in the reviewed released snapshot; it does not establish the precise code version used for published experiments or quantify any score impact.

proposition.claim:
For any feature map the solution has epsilon retrieval throughout each memory neighborhood, and the proposed normalized exponential feature map yields the prescribed dense/sparse Hopfield rule as the SVR optimizer.

The stated exponential upper bound uses the gap <xi_mu,x>-max_{nu!=mu}<xi_mu,xi_nu>.

Sparse retrieval error is no greater than dense retrieval error, which is used to support improved convergence and fixed-point conclusions.

A sufficient separation condition underlies the spherical-memory exponential-capacity derivation.

Released sparse retrieval implements the paper's normalization over the retained memory support.

repair.content:
Restrict the constraint guarantee to sampled inputs and retain learned dual coefficients in the representer solution. No general neighborhood theorem or equality to prescribed softmax weights is certified.

For noiseless keys/values, retained target and fixed mask, define g=<x,xi_mu>-max_{j retained,j!=mu}<x,xi_j> and q=(k-1)exp(-beta*g). Then ||T-xi_mu||<=2m q/(1+q)<=2m(k-1)exp(-beta*g); k=1 gives exact retrieval. The report supplies the complete probability-ratio and triangle-inequality proof.

No universal sparse/dense error ordering is proposed. Specific configurations and independently justified fixed-support convergence remain possible.

No corrected capacity constant or probability theorem is claimed.

Mask excluded logits with negative infinity or normalize only selected original logits, retaining at least one item. For the random method use a boolean support without dropout's logit rescaling. The k=1 example then yields exact target output. Experimental consequences remain unmeasured.
